name: Mandya
headline: Mandya recorded the state's most child marriages since 2020, despite strong SSLC results.
summary: Women and Child Welfare data show 172 child marriages in Mandya in 2020-2023, the highest in the state, with officials also citing single-parent households' financial strain as a driver of irregular attendance. The district's SSLC pass rate was 96.7% in 2023, which hides students who left earlier. Child marriages fell to 25 in January-October 2025 after intensive interventions.

reasons.detail: Mandya recorded 172 child marriages in 2020-2023, the most in the state, falling to 25 by late 2025 after enforcement.
A legislative reply named single-parent households among the reasons for school dropout in Mandya and five other educational districts.
The 2013-14 survey attributed dropout to illiterate parents, poverty and scarcity of rural labour; children were taken to work in hotels and small factories, girls as domestic help.
Families from northern districts migrate to Mandya for the October-March cane harvest; accompanying school-age children are reported to lose about six months of schooling.
Child-protection officials say girls who stay out of school are quickly thought of as ready for marriage; Mandya is cited for frequent child marriages in wedding months.
Responsibility for looking after siblings and girls sent to work as domestic help were listed among causes of children staying away from school.

headlines.takeaway: Seasonal sugarcane migrant children in Mandya go without schooling for months; promised temporary tent schools had not materialised, per the headline and report.

headlines.title: 2,151 school dropouts in Mandya district
headlines.takeaway: A 2013-14 survey found 2,151 out-of-school children aged 6-14, more boys than girls, blaming poverty, migration and illiteracy.

responses.text: The District Child Protection Officer's interventions are reported to have cut child marriages to 25 in the first ten months of 2025.
Free textbooks, uniforms, Ksheera Bhagya and midday meals existed, yet officials were reported as unable to retain children in school (2013-14 coverage).
